**Top 5 U.S. universities by endowment (FY 2022 – the most recent full‑year data publicly available; figures are rounded to the nearest $0.1 billion)**  

| Rank | University | Endowment (billions USD) | FY‑end (as reported) |
|------|------------|--------------------------|----------------------|
| 1 | Harvard University (MA) | **$49.4 B** | FY 2022 |
| 2 | Yale University (CT) | **$41.4 B** | FY 2022 |
| 3 | Stanford University (CA) | **$36.3 B** | FY 2022 |
| 4 | Princeton University (NJ) | **$35.8 B** | FY 2022 |
| 5 | Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MA) | **$24.7 B** | FY 2022 |

**Source** – “List of colleges and universities in the United States by endowment,” Wikipedia (data drawn from the National Association of College and University Business Officers (NACUBO) FY 2022 report).  

### Why FY 2022 is used for “2023”
* The most recent audited, campus‑wide endowment totals that universities publicly release are for fiscal year 2022 (ending June 30 2022).  
* Endowment reports are typically published a year after the fiscal year closes, so the FY 2022 numbers are the latest figures that were available throughout 2023.  
* As of the time of writing (late 2025), FY 2023 endowment totals have not been compiled and released by NACUBO or the individual institutions, so FY 2022 remains the best reliable benchmark.

If you need a projection for FY 2023, a simple “average growth” approach (≈ 3‑5 % annual increase for the largest endowments) would put the numbers roughly at:

| University | Projected FY 2023 endowment* |
|------------|------------------------------|
| Harvard | ~$51 B |
| Yale | ~$43 B |
| Stanford | ~$38 B |
| Princeton | ~$37 B |
| MIT | ~$26 B |

\*These are illustrative estimates only; actual FY 2023 figures may differ once the official reports are released.
